svg.title: Kafka high watermark explained
svg.desc: Shows what high watermark is, how it moves as followers replicate, what consumers can and cannot read, and why it protects against data loss on leader failover.

g.text: High Watermark = highest offset replicated to ALL ISR members

svg.text: Consumer can ONLY read up to the High Watermark
Events above HW are written on leader but not yet replicated — unsafe to read. Could be lost on failover.

g.text: How High Watermark moves — as followers catch up

svg.text: Followers pull from leader continuously. As they replicate offset 7, 8, 9:
HW = minimum of all ISR members' latest offset. Moves forward as EVERYONE catches up.

g.text: Why HW protects against data loss on leader failover

svg.text: Leader B1 has offset 9. B2,B3 only replicated up to 6. HW=6. B1 crashes.
HW vs LEO — two important terms

g.text: Latest offset written on THIS broker

svg.text: HW = safety line. Consumer never reads ahead of HW. LEO = where each broker currently is.
